applied.problem: The worked example says the maker corrects only above 30 °C, but its manual also raises the float below 10 °C, and it contradicts the explanation; the rule is about cell temperature, not the room's.

Single-source figures are stated as universal: 3 to 5 per cent is one rule (BU), 2.33 to 2.40 V boost is one maker's, and 2.50 V equalise is one rule (the same maker equalises at 2.33 to 2.40 V); the gassing line lacked its citation [^4].
Screen 3's hint states the 3 to 5 per cent rule as a definition of full, and screen 5's hint says 110 V puts nothing in, which holds only for a charged battery, not a deeply discharged one.
A tyre does not hold its pressure for good once filled; it slowly loses some, which is why it is checked regularly, as the analogy itself says.

notes.problem: "Cells in a 12 V block" (6) cites source 11, whose quote is about primary and secondary cells and does not state six cells; research R47 (six 2 V cells make 12 V) supports it but is not in the lesson's sources.
Screen 13 and the equalise mark use 2.50 V a cell (BU); the cited maker equalises its vented cells at 2.33 to 2.40 V for up to 72 hours, so the right answer's 2.50 V is one rule, not every maker's.

The float band mixes one maker's 2.23 V at 20 °C with BU's 2.25 to 2.27 V at 25 °C, while the temperature slider applies BU's charge-voltage coefficient about 25 °C to the float; fine as a sketch, but the references differ.
